description.value: The study examined hierarchical organization of scripts using fMRI in healthy young adults and behavioral and structural MRI evidence from patients with focal neurodegenerative disease.

spans.text: The present study examined the organization of complex familiar activities, known as “scripts” (e.g., “going fishing”).

value: We observed significantly greater activation in bilateral inferior frontal regions during judgments of Within-Hierarchy pairs of events compared with Different-Hierarchy event pairs.

The images in each subject's time series were registered to the initial image in the series. The images were then aligned to a standard coordinate system using the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI)152 average brain template. The data were spatially smoothed with an 8-mm full-width half-maximum (FWHM) isotropic Gaussian kernel to facilitate statistical analyses and to account for local variations in activation and sulcal anatomy across participants. Low-pass temporal filtering was implemented by controlling autocorrelation with a first-order autoregressive method.
